reserves.name: Rootstock BTC (rBTC) collateral
reserves.issuerOrObligor: Money on Chain protocol contract on Rootstock (rBTC two-way-peg BTC)

reserveReview.rationale: DOC is backed solely by rBTC locked in the Money on Chain protocol contract, with BPRO absorbing BTC/USD volatility by design; there is no fiat, T-bill, or stablecoin component. At Rootstock block 9,080,700 (hash 0x724d88376c86934387d39f8b7f65c7cec3f4030807765ef514111847115fdeed; 2026-07-22 19:16:34 UTC), eth_getBalance for MoC proxy 0xf773B590aF754D597770937Fa8ea7AbDf2668370 returned 292.636933857635580544 rBTC, while an eth_call of totalSupply() on DOC 0xE700691Da7b9851F2F35f8b8182C69C53ccad9DB returned 3,203,057.992378573495716782 DOC. These pinned reads confirm the single fully on-chain-verifiable reserve asset class without relying on the degraded statistics API.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Money on Chain protocol design (single-asset rBTC collateral) confirmed against Rootstock contract and token state
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: No reserve asset class is unclassified; the only collateral is rBTC in the MoC contract. The legacy MoC statistics API is degraded (catalog responds, measurement endpoints return not-found), so ongoing balances are read directly from chain state.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: rBTC is Rootstock's two-way-peg bitcoin, an exogenous cryptoasset rather than a tracked stablecoin dependency.

sources.label: Money on Chain main-RBTC contract repository

custodyProfile.uncertainty: All collateral sits in the single MoC system contract, an upgradeable proxy, so contract-admin action is the operative custody risk rather than a custodian. The protocol does not lend out collateral by design, but no legal segregation, bankruptcy-remoteness, or rehypothecation terms exist for contract custody. Public code audits in the official repository date to 2019.
